text:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion A : Permanganate titrations are not performed in presence of hydrochloric acid.

Reason R : Chlorine is formed as a consequence of oxidation of hydrochloric acid.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{R}$ are true and $\mathrm{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\mathrm{A}$
Both $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{R}$ are true but $\mathrm{R}$ is NOT the correct explanation of $\mathrm{A}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Assertion A is true: permanganate titrations are carried out in dilute $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$, not in hydrochloric acid.

Reason R is true: acidified permanganate oxidises chloride ions to chlorine.

$2~\mathrm{KMnO}{}_{4}+16\mathrm{HCl}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{KCl}+2\mathrm{MnCl}{}_{2}+8\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}+5\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}$

Part of the permanganate is then used up by HCl instead of by the substance being titrated, so the titre comes out too high; this side reaction is the reason HCl is avoided, so R correctly explains A.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift

text:
Match List I with List II

  
    
    List - I (Complex)
    
    List - II (Hybridization)
  

  
    (A)
    $Ni(CO)_{4}$
    (I)
    $sp^{3}$
  
  
    (B)
    $[Ni(CN)_{4}]^{2-}$
    (II)
    $sp^{3}d^{2}$
  
  
    (C)
    $[Co(CN)_{6}]^{3-}$
    (III)
    $d^{2}sp^{3}$
  
  
    (D)
    $[CoF_{6}]^{3-}$
    (IV)
    $dsp^{2}$
  

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{4}$: Ni(0) is $3d^{8}4s^{2}$; CO shifts the 4s electrons into 3d ($3d^{10}$), leaving 4s and 4p empty, so the hybridisation is $sp^{3}$ (tetrahedral): A-I.

$[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{4}]{}^{2-}$: $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{8}$; strong-field $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ pairs the electrons and frees one 3d orbital, so the hybridisation is $dsp^{2}$ (square planar): B-IV.

$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{6}]{}^{3-}$: $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$ is $3d^{6}$; strong-field $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ pairs all six electrons in three 3d orbitals, freeing two inner 3d orbitals, so the hybridisation is $d^{2}sp^{3}$: C-III.

$[\mathrm{CoF}{}_{6}]{}^{3-}$: weak-field $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$ causes no pairing in $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$ ($3d^{6}$, 4 unpaired electrons), so the outer 4d orbitals are used and the hybridisation is $sp^{3}d^{2}$: D-II.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift

text:
The major product in the given reaction is


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
With $\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$ and heat, the tertiary $-\mathrm{OH}$ of 2,7-dimethyloct-6-en-2-ol is protonated and lost as water, giving a tertiary carbocation at C-2.

The C-6=C-7 double bond attacks this cation through C-6, closing a five-membered ring (C-2 to C-6) and leaving the positive charge on C-7, which is tertiary; attack through C-7 would close a six-membered ring but leave a less stable secondary cation on C-6.

The resulting cation is a cyclopentane with a gem-dimethyl ring carbon (former C-2) next to a ring carbon that carries the exocyclic $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{C}{}^{+}$ group.

$\mathrm{Br}{}^{-}$ from $\mathrm{HBr}$ captures this tertiary cation (any alkene formed by loss of $\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$ adds $\mathrm{HBr}$ by Markovnikov's rule to give the same bromide), giving 1-(2-bromopropan-2-yl)-2,2-dimethylcyclopentane.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift

text:
If the wavelength for an electron emitted from $\mathrm{H}$-atom is $3.3\times 10^{-10}\mathrm{m}$, then energy absorbed by the electron in its ground state compared to minimum energy required for its escape from the atom, is $_________$ times. (Nearest integer)

$[\;$ Given $:\mathrm{h}=6.626\times 10^{-34}\mathrm{J}\mathrm{s}$ ]

Mass of electron $=9.1\times 10^{-31}\mathrm{kg}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Momentum of the emitted electron from the de Broglie relation:

$p=\dfrac{h}{λ}=\dfrac{6.626\times 10^{-34}}{3.3\times 10^{-10}}=2.01\times 10^{-24}\text{kg m s}^{-1}$

Its kinetic energy:

$KE=\dfrac{p^{2}}{2m}=\dfrac{(2.01\times 10^{-24})^{2}}{2\times 9.1\times 10^{-31}}=2.22\times 10^{-18}\text{J}$

The minimum energy for escape from the ground state is the ionization energy of H, $13.6\text{eV}=2.18\times 10^{-18}\text{J}$.

Energy absorbed $=2.18\times 10^{-18}+2.22\times 10^{-18}=4.40\times 10^{-18}\text{J}$.

$\dfrac{4.40\times 10^{-18}}{2.18\times 10^{-18}}=2.02\approx 2$

Hence, the answer is 2.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift

text: A gaseous mixture of two substances A and B, under a total pressure of $0.8$ atm is in equilibrium with an ideal liquid solution. The mole fraction of substance A is $0.5$ in the vapour phase and $0.2$ in the liquid phase. The vapour pressure of pure liquid $\mathrm{A}$ is $__________$ atm. (Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given that $X_{A}=0.2,Y_{A}=0.5,P_{T}=0.8\mathrm{atm}$

We know that $P_{A}=Y_{A}\times P_{T}$

$P_{A}=0.5\times 0.8=0.4$

Now $P_{A}=X_{A}\times P_{A}^{\circ }\Rightarrow P_{A}^{\circ }=\frac{0.4}{0.2}=2\mathrm{atm}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift

text:
At $600\mathrm{K},2\mathrm{mol}$ of $\mathrm{NO}$ are mixed with $1\mathrm{mol}$ of $\mathrm{O}_{2}$.

$2\mathrm{NO}_{(\mathrm{g})}+\mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{g})⇄2\mathrm{NO}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$

The reaction occurring as above comes to equilibrium under a total pressure of 1 atm. Analysis of the system shows that $0.6\mathrm{mol}$ of oxygen are present at equilibrium. The equilibrium constant for the reaction is $________. ($Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

Partial pressure of $\mathrm{NO}(\mathrm{g})=\frac{1.2}{2.6}\times 1$

Partial pressure of $\mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{g})=\frac{0.6}{2.6}$

Partial pressure of $\mathrm{NO}_{2}(\mathrm{g})=\frac{0.8}{2.6}$

$\begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}=\dfrac{(\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{NO}_{2}})^{2}}{(\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{NO}})^{2}(\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{O}_{2}})} & =\dfrac{0.8\times 0.8\times 2.6}{1.2\times 1.2\times 0.6} \\  \\ =1.925 \\  \\ \approx 2 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift

text:
A sample of $0.125\mathrm{g}$ of an organic compound when analyzed by Duma's method yields $22.78\mathrm{mL}$ of nitrogen gas collected over $\mathrm{KOH}$ solution at $280\mathrm{K}$ and $759\mathrm{mm}\mathrm{Hg}$. The percentage of nitrogen in the given organic compound is $__________. ($Nearest integer)

Given :

(a) The vapour pressure of water of $280\mathrm{K}$ is $14.2\mathrm{mm}\mathrm{Hg}$.

(b) $\mathrm{R}=0.082\mathrm{L}$ atm $\mathrm{K}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 28th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$P_{\text{actual}}=759-14.2=744.8\mathrm{mmHg}$

$\begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{N}_{2}} & =\dfrac{744.8\times 22.78}{760\times 0.0821\times 280\times 1000} \\  \\ =0.000971\mathrm{mol} \end{array}$

Mass of $\mathrm{N}_{2}=0.02719\mathrm{gm}$

Percentage of nitrogen

$=\frac{0.0271}{0.125}\times 100=21.75\simeq 22$
